newsitem.title: GERMANY: Action needed on high German wages-wise men.
newsitem.headline: Action needed on high German wages-wise men.

text.p: Germany must move away from its productivity-based wage system, which functions best in times of full employment, to restore balance to its unemployment-hit economy, an independent advisory panel said on Friday.

The five "wise men" group of economists said action should be taken over the next three or four years. Wage rises should lag inflation, and in times of job losses, productivity rises should not be factored into pay rounds.

German unemployment has hit a post-unification high of more than four million, on a seasonally adjusted basis. Meanwhile labour costs are regarded by employers as too high and are hampering investment and driving jobs abroad.
Many German wages are set by industry-wide bargaining, but the panel called for more scope to set wages at the company level.
A recent federal law allows for cuts of 20 percent in sick pay entitlements but has been blocked from implementation due to trade union hostility.
The panel called for agreement on the issue in order to help reduce the cost burden on employers.
